title: A billing problem freezes an apparent subscription
mechanism_summary: A branded email says an account is on hold because payment information needs updating. Its link collects information for scammers rather than resolving a real billing issue.
suggested_beats: A service appears to suspend access.
The fix asks for payment details.
Open the service independently.
why_it_works: Fear of losing access makes the linked fix feel urgent.

title: A refund registration captures private details
mechanism_summary: A message says the recipient qualifies for a government refund and must register through a link. The refund story is a pretext for stealing personal or financial information.
suggested_beats: An unexpected refund is announced.
Registration requests sensitive information.
Verify refunds through the official agency.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone hoping to receive a refund
why_it_works: An unexpected benefit can lower scrutiny of the information requested.

title: An unfamiliar invoice hides a malicious attachment
mechanism_summary: A scam email presents an invoice the recipient does not recognize. Opening its attachment or following its payment link can expose information or introduce malware.
suggested_beats: An invoice arrives unexpectedly.
The attachment becomes the trap.
Verify the sender before opening files.
why_it_works: Routine administrative work can encourage opening a document before checking it.

title: An overdue toll text copies an agency
mechanism_summary: A text claims the recipient owes a road toll and threatens extra charges. It links to a website impersonating the toll service.
suggested_beats: A small toll debt is announced.
The link imitates the collection agency.
Check toll accounts through an independently found site.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone worried about a missed toll
why_it_works: A small debt paired with a penalty can prompt quick compliance.

title: A mystery gift contains a phishing QR code
mechanism_summary: An unexpected package contains a QR code that appears to explain who sent it. Scanning can lead to a website seeking account or card information.
suggested_beats: An unexplained package arrives.
Its explanation requires scanning a code.
Do not enter credentials through an unexpected package link.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone curious about an unsolicited gift
why_it_works: Curiosity gives a malicious link a plausible physical invitation.

title: A prospective buyer demands identity verification
mechanism_summary: A supposed buyer asks an online seller to share a texted verification code. The code actually helps register a calling account linked to the seller's number.
suggested_beats: A buyer expresses interest.
The buyer requires a verification code.
Keep account verification codes private.
why_it_works: A demand to prove honesty reverses suspicion onto the legitimate seller.

title: A missing-pet reply asks for a code
mechanism_summary: A scammer responding to a lost-pet notice claims to have found the animal. Before arranging its return, the scammer requests a verification code used to set up a calling account.
suggested_beats: A hopeful reply claims the pet is found.
Returning it depends on sharing a code.
Verify the claim without sharing account codes.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone searching for a missing pet
why_it_works: Relief and urgency can overwhelm scrutiny of an unrelated security request.

title: An account warning becomes a remote-support call
mechanism_summary: A pop-up claims a device has a serious security problem and supplies a support contact. The apparent support agent seeks remote access or payment for an invented repair.
suggested_beats: A warning interrupts browsing.
Calling it leads to remote-access instructions.
Use the real provider's support channel.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone alarmed by a device warning
why_it_works: An alarming screen makes an unsolicited helper appear necessary.
